title: Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 17: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559 (dated 1794) via OPenn + Sanskrit and English of Annie Besant, The Bhagavad-Gita (4th ed. 1922), Wikisource
description: Bhagavad Gita chapter 17 (The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith), shown page by page on a Sanskrit manuscript copied in 1794 (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559), with the Sanskrit text and Annie Besant's English.
introduction:
The Bhagavad Gita ("Song of the Lord") is a dialogue of 700 verses between the prince Arjuna and Krishna, set on the battlefield of Kurukshetra in book 6 (Bhishmaparvan) of the Mahabharata. Its date of composition is debated; many scholars place it in the last centuries BCE. This is chapter 17, The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith (28 verses as numbered in the manuscript and in Besant's edition).

The pages shown are from a complete Sanskrit manuscript of the Gita at the University of Pennsylvania (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559), 90 paper leaves of 7 lines in Devanagari, with speaker headings, colophons and verse-end marks in red. Its final colophon (fol. 90r) dates the copy to Saṃvat 1851, the third day of the bright half of Caitra (1794 CE). Chapter 17 runs from fol. 77r to the chapter colophon on fol. 80v.

Each section below is one manuscript page: the verses whose text ends on that page, located by reading the scribe's verse numbers and the first and last words on the image. When a verse begins at the foot of one page and ends on the next, both pages are shown. The Sanskrit and English are from Annie Besant's edition and translation (4th edition, 1922), which prints each verse in Devanagari with its English; the manuscript's spelling differs from the printed text in small details.
translator_notes: Sanskrit and English: Annie Besant, The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th edition (Madras: G. A. Natesan, 1922), transcription validated on English Wikisource. Besant's footnotes are not reproduced.

Verse numbers follow Besant and the manuscript, which agree throughout: chapter 13 counts Arjuna's opening question ('prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva...') as verse 1, so it has 35 verses and the whole text 701.

K. T. Telang's translation (Sacred Books of the East 8, 1882) was the first choice for the English, but it is continuous prose without verse divisions, so it cannot be matched to manuscript pages verse by verse; Besant's verse-numbered translation is used instead.

The last section of each chapter is the chapter colophon. Besant prints most Sanskrit colophons in shortened form (marked with ॰) while her English gives the full formula; the manuscript writes the colophon out in full, and its chapter names differ in places from Besant's (see the scan note).

In the Wikisource transcription of Besant's edition, the verse-number label is irregular at 17.19 (printed or transcribed as '(20)'). The verses are counted in sequence and checked against the Sanskrit numbers, which are regular.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.1-3; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 77r
translation.original_text:
1अर्जुन उवाच ।
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः ।
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥ १ ॥

2श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥ २ ॥

3सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत ।
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥ ३ ॥
translation.text:
1Arjuna said:
Those that sacrifice full of faith, but casting aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, what is verily their condition, O Krishna? Is it one of Purity, Passion, or Darkness?

2The Blessed Lord said:
Threefold is by nature the inborn faith of the embodied—pure, passionate, and dark. Hear thou of these.

3The faith of each is shaped to his own nature, O Bhârata. The man consists of his faith; that which his faith is, he is even that.
translation.scan_note: fol. 77r, OPenn image 6555_0076 (lower leaf). Checked on the image: colophon of ch. 16 ends line 1 '-rjunasaṃvāde daivāsurasaṃpadvibhāgayogo nāma ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||16||'; arjuna uvāca line 2; ||1|| line 3, ||2|| line 5, ||3|| line 6; 17.4 begins line 7.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.4-7; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 77r and fol. 77v
translation.original_text:
4यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः ।
प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥ ४ ॥

5अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।
दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥ ५ ॥

6कर्शयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः ।
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥ ६ ॥

7आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः ।
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥ ७ ॥
translation.text:
4Pure men worship the Gods; the passionate the gnomes and giants; the others, the dark folk, worship ghosts and troops of nature-spirits.

5The men who perform severe austerities, unenjoined by the Scriptures, wedded to vanity and egoism, impelled by the force of their desires and passions,

6Unintelligent, tormenting the aggregated elements forming the body, and Me also, seated in the inner body, know these demoniacal in their resolves.

7The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.
translation.scan_note: fol. 77v, OPenn image 6555_0077 (upper leaf). Checked on the image: ||4|| line 2 ... ||7|| line 7. Verse 17.4 begins on the previous page, fol. 77r, so both pages are shown.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.8-11; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 77v and fol. 78r
translation.original_text:
8आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः ।
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥ ८ ॥

9कट्‌वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः ।
आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥ ९ ॥

10यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥ १० ॥

11अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टोय इज्यते ।
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥ ११ ॥
translation.text:
8The foods that augment vitality, energy, vigour, health, joy and cheerfulness, delicious, bland, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the pure.

9The passionate desire foods that are bitter, sour, saline, over-hot, pungent, dry and burning and which produce pain, grief and sickness.

10That which is stale and flat, putrid and corrupt, leavings also and unclean, is the food dear to the dark.

11The sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for fruit, as enjoined by the ordinances, under the firm belief that sacrifice is a duty, that is pure.
translation.scan_note: fol. 78r, OPenn image 6555_0077 (lower leaf). Checked on the image: ||8|| line 2 ... ||11|| line 7. Verse 17.8 begins on the previous page, fol. 77v, so both pages are shown.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.12-15; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 78r and fol. 78v
translation.original_text:
12अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ १२ ॥

13विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥ १३ ॥

14देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ।
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥ १४ ॥

15अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥ १५ ॥
translation.text:
12The sacrifice offered with a view verily to fruit, and also indeed for self-glorification, O best of the Bhâratas; know thou that to be of passion.

13The sacrifice contrary to the ordinances, without distributing food, devoid of words of power and without gifts, empty of faith, is said to be of darkness.

14Worship given to the Gods, to the twice-born, to the teachers and to the wise, purity, straightforwardness, continence and harmlessness, are called the austerity of the body.

15Speech causing no annoyance, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Scriptures, are called the austerity of speech.
translation.scan_note: fol. 78v, OPenn image 6555_0078 (upper leaf). Checked on the image: ||12|| line 1 ... ||15|| line 6. Verse 17.12 begins on the previous page, fol. 78r, so both pages are shown.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.16-19; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 78v and fol. 79r
translation.original_text:
16मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥ १६ ॥

17श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः ।
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥ १७ ॥

18सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥ १८ ॥

19मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः ।
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ १९ ॥
translation.text:
16Mental happiness, equilibrium, silence, self-control, purity of nature—these are called the austerity of the mind.

17This threefold austerity, performed by men with the utmost faith, without desire for fruit, harmonised, is said to be pure.

18The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining respect, honour and worship, and for ostentation, is said to be of passion, unstable and fleeting.

19That austerity done under a deluded understanding, with self-torture, or with the object of destroying another, that is declared of darkness.
translation.scan_note: fol. 79r, OPenn image 6555_0078 (lower leaf). Checked on the image: ||16|| line 1 ... ||19|| line 6. Verse 17.16 begins on the previous page, fol. 78v, so both pages are shown.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.20-23; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 79r and fol. 79v
translation.original_text:
20दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥ २० ॥

21यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ २१ ॥

22अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥

23ओं तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ।
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥ २३ ॥
translation.text:
20That alms given to one who does nothing in return, believing that a gift ought to be made in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that alms is accounted pure.

21That given with a view to receiving in return, or looking for fruit again, or grudgingly, that alms is accounted of passion.

22That alms given at unfit place and time, and to unworthy persons, disrespectfully and contemptuously, that is declared of darkness.

23"Aum Tat Sat," this has been considered to be the threefold designation of the Eternal. By that were ordained of old Brâhmanas, Vedas and sacrifices.
translation.scan_note: fol. 79v, OPenn image 6555_0079 (upper leaf). Checked on the image: ||20|| line 1 ... ||23|| line 6. Verse 17.20 begins on the previous page, fol. 79r, so both pages are shown.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.24-27; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 79v and fol. 80r
translation.original_text:
24तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः ।
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥ २४ ॥

25तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः ।
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥ २५ ॥

26सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते ।
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥ २६ ॥

27यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥ २७ ॥
translation.text:
24Therefore with the pronunciation of "Aum" the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as laid down in the ordinances are always commenced by the knowers of the Eternal.

25With the pronunciation of "Tat" and without aiming at fruit are performed the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and gift, by those desiring liberation.

26"Sat" is used in the sense of reality and goodness; likewise, O Pârtha, the word "Sat" is used in the sense of a good work.

27Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift is also called "Sat", and action for the sake of the Supreme is also named "Sat."
translation.scan_note: fol. 80r, OPenn image 6555_0079 (lower leaf). Checked on the image: ||24|| line 1 ... ||27|| line 6. Verse 17.24 begins on the previous page, fol. 79v, so both pages are shown.

translation.original_ref: Bhagavad Gita 17.28; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 80r and fol. 80v
translation.original_text:
28अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥ २८ ॥
translation.text: 28Whatsoever is wrought without faith, oblation, gift, austerity, or other deed, "Asat" it is called, O Pârtha; it is nought, here or hereafter.
translation.scan_note: fol. 80v, OPenn image 6555_0080 (upper leaf). Checked on the image: ||28|| line 1; colophon lines 1-3 '... guṇavibhāgadarśano nāma saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||17||'; arjuna uvāca line 3; 18.1 ends line 5 (||1||), 18.2 ends line 7 (||2||); 18.3 begins line 7. Verse 17.28 begins on the previous page, fol. 80r, so both pages are shown.

translation.original_ref: Colophon of chapter 17; Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 559, fol. 80v
translation.text: Thus in the glorious Upanishads of the Bhagavad-Gita, the science of the Eternal, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Shrî Krishna and Arjuna, the seventeenth discourse, entitled: THE YOGA OF THE DIVISION OF THREEFOLD FAITH.
translation.scan_note: fol. 80v: ||28|| line 1; colophon lines 1-3 '... guṇavibhāgadarśano nāma saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||17||'; arjuna uvāca line 3; 18.1 ends line 5 (||1||), 18.2 ends line 7 (||2||); 18.3 begins line 7. The manuscript names the chapter guṇavibhāgadarśana; the Sanskrit and English shown are the colophon printed in Besant's edition, whose wording differs in places from the manuscript's.
